description: A challenging team made of Physics students that are willing to go to the end of the world to learn
summary:
SILENT WORLDS: The Forgotten Machines of the Moon, Mars & Beyond is an interactive 3D web journey that tells the dramatic story of 13 real space robots left resting across our solar system. Spanning from Surveyor 1’s soft Moon landing in 1966 to Ingenuity’s groundbreaking flight on Mars in 2021, the platform turns unmanned space exploration into a gripping, cinematic narrative.

Built to engage high school students and space fans without overwhelming them with textbook clutter, the site organizes every mission around four clear themes: who created the craft, why it was launched into deep space, the bold engineering milestone it achieved, and the lasting legacy it left behind.

On screen, every spacecraft is presented as a hands-on 3D model that users can rotate and explore at true-to-life scale, complete with built-in WebXR Augmented Reality that lets students place life-sized replicas right onto their classroom or living room floors. Instead of offering scattered facts, the timeline flows like a cosmic relay race—illustrating how early Moon landers laid the groundwork for deep-space probes, orbital telescopes, and Mars rovers—transforming metal and solar panels into unsung pioneers standing forever at the frontier of discovery.
details:
SILENT WORLDS: The Forgotten Machines of the Moon, Mars & Beyond is an interactive 3D website that tells the story of 13 real space robots left behind across our solar system between 1966 and 2021. Built using modern web tools like React and Three.js, the site lets users spin and zoom around detailed 3D models of famous rovers, landers, and telescopes. With built-in Augmented Reality (AR), students can even scan a QR code on their phone to place life-sized spacecraft right onto their classroom or bedroom floor without downloading an app. Instead of acting like a boring list of facts, the site calculates real distances from Earth and communication delays while breaking each mission down into clear, exciting parts: who built the craft, why it launched, what it discovered, and how it finally went quiet.

Made for high school students and space fans, the project brings dry textbook dates and measurements to life with a smooth, easy-to-use design inspired by Neal.fun. Our team turned real NASA and JPL research into fast-paced, dramatic stories—covering the big risks, major breakthroughs, and final farewells—to honor these machines as brave explorers. By making sure the website works well on both computers and phones, keeps the AR sizes completely accurate, and blends hands-on 3D models with great storytelling, SILENT WORLDS helps students truly picture the scale of space and inspires the next generation of engineers and scientists.
